content:
Earlier this month, Google released the new Pixel 11 series phones. Compared to last year's Pixel 10 series, the phones themselves haven't changed much, but they offer some welcome improvements in user experience. One of these is a new set of camera processing options, allowing you to take much greater control over the final look of your photos.

On the eve of the iPhone 18 Pro launch, I hope Apple offers something similar.

The Pixel 11 adds a new camera feature called Camera Looks. This is somewhat similar to Photographic Styles on the iPhone, which let you adjust how the camera captures images before you press the shutter. These adjustments are made before the shot is taken, so they're more than just regular filters.

Google offers many presets similar to Apple's, and even lets you fine-tune the details of each one. There are also several options that capture new trends in fluid photography: Editorial, Velvet, Classic, Digi, Black Tie, and Minimal.

These styles all veer away from the heavily polished look of smartphone photos, trying instead to recapture the charm of old-fashioned photography. Digi, true to its name, recreates the low dynamic range, high contrast, and noisy imaging style of those lightweight pocket cameras from the 2010s.

On the other end, Minimal goes fully low-processing — much of the HDR processing pipeline doesn't run, so you get basically what the smartphone sensor actually captured. You can see some sample photos over at 9to5Google.

Using the ProRAW format on iPhone can certainly bring photos back to a state with less post-processing applied. But doing so somewhat defeats the purpose of shooting with a phone.

Summary

If Apple wants to build the best camera you can carry in your pocket, it has to accept that not every user has the same needs. Photographic Styles was a good start, but Apple should go further. Photography is ultimately an art of self-expression, and giving users more options to control how much processing is applied to their photos would be a huge step forward. Apple should borrow from Google and add a 'Minimal' style to the iPhone.

What do you think about the current state of iPhone photography? Do you like how Apple has handled Photographic Styles lately, or do you feel there's still room for improvement? Let us know in the comments.
